subject: SLA template exception request — uptime & monthly remedy cap (CloudNova)
messages:
From: Susan Park <susan@cloudnova.com>
To: logan.wright@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@cloudnova.com
Date: 2026-05-06T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: SLA template exception request — uptime & monthly remedy cap

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's ability to keep latency tight on our inference-heavy routes. We are making progress internally but have a configuration question on the standard SLA template.

CloudNova runs mixed workloads (interactive + nightly batch ingestion). For a number of our batch-only routes we need:
- a lower uptime floor (we're asking to move from 99.95% to 99.9% for specific non-interactive routes)
- a hard cap on monthly service credits tied to those routes (our procurement team wants an upper bound of 10% of the monthly invoice for those carve-outs)

Can Redwood accept route-level SLA carveouts (cataloged in the SOW) rather than a blanket amendment to the global uptime figure? If so, can you confirm how monthly remedy would be computed for those routes (per-route uptime or combined footprint)? Also attaching our completed SLA-exception-request-form for your SOC team to review.

We'd like to get this finalized alongside the SOW so we can proceed to signatures next week.

Thanks,
Susan Park
Head of Procurement
CloudNova Systems

Attachment: SLA-exception-request-form.pdf
From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: Susan Park <susan@cloudnova.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-05-06T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: SLA template exception request — uptime & monthly remedy cap

Hi Susan — appreciate the clear ask and the form. I'm looping in Karthik (sales lead) and Laura (legal) so we can align on pricing/contract mechanics and the operational carveouts.

High level response:
- We can support route-level SLA carveouts pinned in the SOW for non-interactive batch routes.
- For carveout routes we'd normally keep the platform-wide availability number in the master agreement (99.95%) but allow an SOW attachment that declares certain routes are scoped to a lower availability floor. Remedy computation would be per-route: monthly uptime percentage for that route, multiplied by that route's billed proportion.

Proposed middle-ground we often use: tiered monthly remedy cap linked to total invoice rather than a per-route absolute. Example (proposal to discuss):
- If carved routes are <= 20% of monthly tokens, cap remedies at 8% of invoice.
- If carved routes are 21-40%, cap remedies at 6% of invoice.
- If carved routes exceed 40%, we need a dedicated capacity commitment (Reserved/Dedicated) and a different pricing band.

This approach keeps incentives aligned (larger carved workloads get stronger operational guarantees via Dedicated) while giving procurement predictability.

For next steps I attached our baseline metrics export so you can confirm the route breakdown and our proposed amendment draft with the SOW clause language. Laura, can you comment on any legal constraints for a per-route repair calculation and the exact wording for the cap?

—Logan

Attachments: baseline-metrics-may2026.csv; proposed-amendment-draft.docx

Quick note from pricing side:
- We can be flexible on the cap but 10% is high relative to our normal maximums. 8% is a reasonable negotiating start for carveouts, assuming CloudNova stays on hosted capacity and doesn't exceed the token ratio bands Logan outlined.
- If they want a 10% hard cap with their current usage split, we'd need to scope in a small Dedicated pod (1-2 GPUs reserved) or a throughput reservation to limit blast radius. That would move them to a committed monthly price and change invoicing.

I'll prepare a short pricing appendix with both options so Susan has clear trade-offs.

—Karthik

Thanks Logan — that tiered-cap approach sounds reasonable. A couple of follow-ups/questions from our end:

1) Latency SLA: for our interactive routes we need the standard latency SLO (p95) to be explicit in the SOW. For the carved batch routes, we are OK if latency is 'best-effort' but we want to ensure those routes are excluded from latency-based remedies. Can the amendment call that out?

2) Remedy calculation: please confirm that per-route uptime uses the route's ingress requests as the denominator (we need to avoid token-weight distortions).

3) Doc signing: once we have language we can route to legal — can you send a DocuSign link and a redline-ready Word file?

If you can confirm the 8% cap as a starting point and send the redline doc + DocuSign link, Procurement will aim to finish approvals by Friday.

Best,
Susan

Susan — thanks. Summary and next steps from Redwood: 

Summary of agreement in principle:
- We will allow route-level SLA carveouts documented in the SOW for non-interactive/batch routes. Those routes may declare a lower uptime floor (e.g., 99.90%) and will be explicitly excluded from latency-based remedies.
- Remedy computation: per-route monthly uptime using ingress-request counts for that route as the denominator, multiplied by that route's billed portion.
- Cap: Redwood will provisionally accept an 8% cap of the monthly invoice for remedies tied to carved routes, contingent on CloudNova staying within the <20% carved-route threshold. If carved-route usage grows beyond thresholds, we'll trigger a scope review and either require Dedicated commitments or change the cap.

Action items:
- Logan: circulate a redline-ready Word with the amendment language and create a DocuSign envelope for signatures (attached draft).
- Karthik: provide the two pricing appendices (hosted w/8% cap vs. small Dedicated pod w/10% cap) by EOD tomorrow.
- Laura: quick legal sanity-check on the per-route repair wording — if no redlines, proceed to DocuSign.

I'll attach the amendment draft and the filled exception form on the DocuSign envelope. If procurement confirms Friday target, we'll prioritize the DocuSign flow.

Thanks — talk soon.
—Logan
